shared_text:
The flight. A wide-body airliner landing at an airport in the early hours of the morning.

The crew. The first officer was the pilot flying and was in line training (initial operating experience) on the aircraft. The captain was the pilot monitoring.

What happened. The crew had briefed a reduced-flap landing. Under their plan, the first officer would let the autobrakes slow the aircraft to below 30 knots and then hand control to the captain, who would make the turn off the runway. During the rollout, while the crew were monitoring the deceleration, the tower controller told them to turn off at a taxiway. The aircraft was just short of that taxiway, and it had not yet slowed enough for control to be handed over and the turn made. The crew judged that the aircraft was too fast to make that turn safely. The first officer looked up and saw that they were passing the taxiway. The crew told the tower that they were unable to make the turn. The controller told them to hurry to the next exit, because there was traffic on short final. The crew tried to be quick and continued along the runway towards the next exit.
safe_outcome: The traffic on short final behind them went around, and the aircraft left the runway at the next exit. No one was hurt and no aircraft was damaged.
bad_outcome: The landing aircraft's crew saw the conflict late and went around from about 50 feet, passing low over this aircraft. A flight attendant on the landing aircraft was thrown off balance by the abrupt go-around and received a minor injury.
notes: Variant B-landing: the conflicting traffic was the aircraft on short final behind, which went around. Bracket 'this aircraft': the aircraft was still on the runway heading for the next exit. Removed under rule 3: the captain's Cause ('late instructions' from the tower); the first officer's Cause and Suggestions (whether it was avoidable, ATC spacing optimised for arrival rate, alerting ATC to training flights). Moved to the safe ending under rule 5: the go-around of the following traffic and the exit at the next taxiway. Dropped as post-event follow-up: the tower asking the captain to telephone afterwards to explain. Removed under rule 6: airport and taxiway names. Judgement calls: aircraft class from A300 (wide-body). No weather or light condition is coded; the 0001-0600 time band is rendered as 'the early hours of the morning'. 'Too fast to make that turn safely' is the captain's account (also what the captain told ATC afterwards), stated as the crew's judgement. 'Initial operating experience' (IOE) kept as the training context; the report's link between training needs and the flap configuration sits in the Cause section and was not used. The safe ending does not say the go-around was 'in good time' because the report does not say so (D4 applied).
